accepted_wording: On 33 fresh prime-order Weierstrass curves (group orders about 2^24, 2^28 and 2^32), T = 1024/4096/16384, 22 paired configurations per cell, counted F_p and mod-n operations (I = 3/10/30 M, S = M) with hash-table and solver operations at 0/0.1/1 GAE: this harness's multi-target index calculus (the cheaper of ic5 and ic5ks per configuration and price; ic5ks's retention of solved trial classes along the shared arithmetic-progression W saves at most 1.5%) costs 1.003-1.810x per target of the cheapest of 15 runs of this harness's multi-target rho per configuration and price (Kuhn-Struik retention rho rho2xks at h = 0 and 0.1, distinguished-point rho rhodp at h = 1) and is dearer in all 27 cell x I/M decisions of the frozen rule; at I = 10M it is 1.04-1.16x at h = 0, 1.03-1.08x at h = 0.1 and 1.20-1.76x at h = 1; it is 1.14-1.49x a paired BSGS. The frozen rule prices h on hash-table operations only: with rhodp's per-step canonicalisations priced at the same h (AGENTS.md section 5a) the IC is 0.89-0.94x the cheapest rho at h = 1 and I = 10M and all 27 decisions are unranked, so no ranking against rho is established.
